intent: The field-styled button that shows the current choice of its Select and opens the popup list.
typical_uses: The visible field of a Select, holding a SelectValue
A compact filter chip in a toolbar, through the `filter` variant

dont_use_when.situation: A button that opens a list of actions

invariants.text: The trigger always appends a chevron icon after its children; there is no prop to remove or replace it.
With the `filter` variant the caption stays in the muted foreground color even after a value is chosen; with the `default` variant only the placeholder is muted.
Setting `aria-invalid="true"` on the trigger switches its border and focus ring to the destructive color, also while it has focus.
select.module.css sizes the trigger to its content (`width: fit-content`); a trigger that should fill its column needs a width from `className`.

anti_patterns.dont: Render the trigger with no accessible name
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `aria-label` on the trigger, or point a Label's `htmlFor` at the trigger's `id`; the trigger is a real button, so a label can name it

a11y.by: the primitive's Select.Trigger renders a button with role combobox, aria-expanded and aria-haspopup="listbox"; select.test.tsx asserts the trigger is found by the combobox role and its aria-label name

children.states: children is the trigger's caption, a SelectValue or text the caller composes
children.because: `React.ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more, which the compiler cannot state as one JSON type.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the trigger's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the trigger's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open, disabled, placeholder, ...). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through select.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.reason: Composed inside SelectTrigger around the kit's fixed chevron; it has no props of its own on the trigger.

good.title: A compact trigger with a placeholder
good.code:
<Select items={REGIONS}>
  <SelectTrigger size="sm" aria-label="Region">
    <SelectValue placeholder="Pick a region" />
  </SelectTrigger>
  <SelectContent>
    <SelectItem value="eu-central">Frankfurt</SelectItem>
  </SelectContent>
</Select>

good.title: A toolbar filter chip with a caption the caller composes
good.code:
<Select value={status} onValueChange={setStatus}>
  <SelectTrigger variant="filter" aria-label="Status filter">
    Status
  </SelectTrigger>
  <SelectContent>
    <SelectItem value="open">Open</SelectItem>
    <SelectItem value="closed">Closed</SelectItem>
  </SelectContent>
</Select>

bad.title: A chevron icon added inside the trigger
bad.why: The trigger already renders its own chevron after its children, so this draws two.

children.description: TS: ReactNode. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. children is the trigger's caption, a SelectValue or text the caller composes. `React.ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more, which the compiler cannot state as one JSON type.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, SelectTriggerState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the trigger's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: SelectTriggerState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function of the trigger's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open, disabled, placeholder, ...). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through select.module.css, not through this.
